I am a 45-year-old farmer in Quzhou County. I have been farming this land for 15 years, and my household has 5 mouths to feed, though some of my family work off-farm and bring in extra cash. My farm is only 1.5 mu, so every decision I make has to count—I cannot afford to waste inputs, but I also cannot afford to under-invest and lose yield. Because I have some schooling, I pay attention to what the agricultural extension station recommends, but at the end of the day, I rely on my own experience and what I see in my fields.

It is now spring, and my winter wheat is already in the ground from last October. The wheat looks decent, but the spring management will decide everything. I will top-dress with nitrogen around the jointing stage and irrigate three times in total for the wheat crop: once as winter irrigation (already done), once at jointing, and once at the grain-filling stage. I use an improved wheat variety that has done well on this land before. For the base fertilizer, I applied compound fertilizer at sowing, and now the spring top-dressing will bring my total nitrogen to about 17 kg per mu. I also make sure to apply phosphorus and potassium because the soil here needs it. I will spray twice—once for weeds and once for pests or disease if I see any. Before last autumn’s sowing, I used rotary tillage to prepare the seedbed after the maize harvest. I expect about 500 kg per mu from this wheat crop if the weather cooperates.

As soon as the wheat comes off in early June, I have a very narrow window to get the summer maize in. Time is money, so I will plant hybrid maize seed using no-tillage direct seeding right after the wheat harvest. I have done this for years—it saves time, keeps soil moisture, and works fine. I apply fertilizer at sowing and then side-dress with nitrogen when the maize is knee-high. I will irrigate twice for the maize because summer rainfall can be unpredictable, and well water is my insurance. I spray herbicide once and maybe an insecticide once if the corn borer shows up. On this small plot, I expect around 550 kg per mu from the hybrid maize.

My labor is limited because some family members are working in town, so I keep things simple and efficient. I do not experiment with strange new varieties or methods on my only 1.5 mu. I stick with what works, manage inputs carefully, and make sure I get both crops in and out on time.
